vignette: A 78-year-old woman with a recent large left putaminal hemorrhage has a transient right hemiparesis. Which anatomical fact explains why hypertensive hemorrhages favor this site?

options.text: The putamen has the richest cortical blood supply
The lateral lenticulostriate arteries are end-arteries arising directly from the high-pressure M1 segment
The putamen lies in a watershed between two territories
The internal capsule has no blood-brain barrier
The putamen is drained by the great cerebral vein

explanation: The lateral lenticulostriate perforators leave the M1 segment at right angles and take its full pressure without collateral support, so chronic hypertension produces lipohyalinosis and Charcot-Bouchard microaneurysms there; their rupture is the putaminal hemorrhage and their occlusion the capsular lacune.
